theme.title: Stars and Surprises
theme.subtitle: Teams, stars and stories from across basketball
theme.recap: The best numbers come from all over basketball history. Which answer surprised you most?

questions.prompt: How many regular-season games did the 2003–04 Pistons win?
questions.note: 54–28, before the defense-first Pistons won the title.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: finishing second in the Central Division with a 54–28 record

funFacts.text: Detroit used its 2003 second-overall draft pick on Darko Miličić, who played a limited reserve role during the title season.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: They selected Darko Miličić as their top pick but only used him as a reserve

funFacts.text: Larry Brown arrived as head coach after Detroit reached the Eastern Conference finals the year before.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: After their first trip to the Conference Finals since 1991, the Pistons hired Larry Brown as head coach.

funFacts.text: The Pistons clinched the title at their home arena, the Palace of Auburn Hills, outside downtown Detroit.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: The Palace of Auburn Hills, Auburn Hills, Michigan

questions.prompt: The 2019–20 Lakers never lost when leading after three quarters. How many such games did they win, playoffs included?
questions.context: Los Angeles Lakers · 2019–20 · regular season plus playoffs

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: to be undefeated in a season when leading entering the fourth quarter, going a combined 57–0 record

funFacts.text: The Lakers–Heat series took place inside the Orlando-area NBA bubble with no paying fans in the building.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: games were played in the Bubble behind closed doors

funFacts.text: Both Finals participants had missed the playoffs the previous year, an unprecedented turnaround for the matchup.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: the first time that Finals participants had both missed the playoffs in the previous season

funFacts.text: Jeanie Buss became the first female controlling owner to guide her team to an NBA title.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Jeanie Buss became the first female controlling owner to guide her team to an NBA title

questions.prompt: Robert Horry hit the game-winner in Game 5 of the 2005 Finals. How many points did he score off the bench?

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Horry went 5 for 6 from beyond the arc, including the game-winner, and scored 21 points coming off the bench.

funFacts.text: Rasheed Wallace left Horry open when he doubled Manu Ginóbili, setting up the decisive shot.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Rasheed Wallace had left Horry to double-team Ginobili

funFacts.text: Horry did not score until the very end of the third quarter before taking over late.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: He hadn't scored a point until the final play of the 3rd quarter

funFacts.text: The shot added to Horry's reputation for late-game heroics, already established with the Lakers.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Horry was already famous for nailing last-second shots in the playoffs

questions.prompt: What did Michael Jordan average per game in the 1993 Finals against Phoenix, a Finals record?
questions.context: 1993 NBA Finals · six games vs Phoenix

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: averaged a Finals-record 41.0 PPG during the six-game series

funFacts.text: The Suns traded Jeff Hornacek, Tim Perry and Andrew Lang to Philadelphia for Charles Barkley.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: acquiring Charles Barkley from the Philadelphia 76ers in exchange for Jeff Hornacek, Tim Perry, and Andrew Lang

funFacts.text: Phoenix forced a rare triple-overtime Game 3, then won it at Chicago Stadium.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: The Phoenix Suns won Game 3 in triple overtime, 129–121

funFacts.text: Scottie Pippen also filled the box score with over nine rebounds and seven assists per game.

questions.prompt: How many playoff games did the 1983 champion Sixers lose?

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: The 76ers completed one of the most dominating playoff runs in league history with a 12–1 mark

funFacts.text: Moses Malone had boldly predicted an unbeaten playoff run, repeatedly calling for four-game sweeps.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Malone predicted the team would win in four games in each of the three rounds

funFacts.text: Philadelphia had acquired Moses from Houston specifically to counter the Lakers' Kareem Abdul-Jabbar.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: the 76ers acquired Moses Malone from the Houston Rockets in an effort to counter Abdul-Jabbar

funFacts.text: The Sixers swept Los Angeles in the Finals, reversing the previous championship-series losses to the Lakers.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: The 76ers lost their first two Finals meetings with the Lakers in 1980 and 1982
